name: tiamat

special_abilities.name: discorporation
special_abilities.desc: When Tiamat drops to 0 hit points or dies, her body is destroyed but her essence travels back to her domain in the Nine Hells, and she is unable to take physical form for a time.

special_abilities.name: innate spellcasting (3/day)
special_abilities.desc: Tiamat can innately cast divine word (spell save DC 26). Her spellcasting ability is Charisma.

special_abilities.name: legendary resistance (5/day)
special_abilities.desc: If Tiamat fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

special_abilities.name: limited magic immunity
special_abilities.desc: Unless she wishes to be affected, Tiamat is immune to spells of 6th level or lower. She has advantage on saving throws against all other spells and magical effects.

special_abilities.name: multiple heads
special_abilities.desc: Tiamat can take one reaction per turn, rather than only one per round. She also has advantage on saving throws against being knocked unconscious. If she fails a saving throw against an effect that would stun a creature, one of her unspent legendary actions is spent.

special_abilities.name: regeneration
special_abilities.desc: Tiamat regains 30 hit points at the start of her turn.

actions.name: multiattack
actions.desc: Tiamat can use her Frightful Presence. She then makes three attacks: two with her claws and one with her tail.

actions.name: claw
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 24 (4d6 + 10) slashing damage.

actions.name: tail
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (4d8 + 10) piercing damage.

lore:
Tiamat is the primordial sovereign of the Chromatic Brood, a multi-headed terror whose presence defies the natural order. She dwells within the sulfurous pits of the Avernian wastes, where the sky bleeds and the earth weeps molten iron. Her predatory nature is not born of mere hunger, but of an insatiable, divine avarice. Each of her five visages—crimson, azure, emerald, ebony, and ivory—strikes with a distinct, catastrophic force, turning entire legions to ash or brittle ice in a single breath.

In local lore, she is the "Bane of Bahamut," a cosmic force of entropy that existed before the first sun. Peasant songs whisper of her as the Mother of Greed; to speak her name is to invite the shadow of wings that span horizons. She does not merely hunt; she reclaims what she believes is her birthright: the entire world. Adventurers are warned: Tiamat is no mere beast to be tracked, but a living apocalypse. To encounter her is not a battle, but a witnessing of the end of days.
